verdict.rationale: Clerk's 'eve' feature set explicitly documents gating tool calls against caller permissions/scopes and brokering OAuth so tools get a provider token 'on the caller's behalf' (clerk-docs-16/27), backed by OAuth scoped-access (clerk-docs-10/29) and M2M/API-key infrastructure for agents (clerk-docs-11) — directly matching the token-vault/delegated-authority story. However, this is documented only as first-party docs with no explicit mention of token short-livedness for these brokered provider tokens, no independent/hands-on validation, and no detail on consent UX or token revocation flow. Missing for 10: independent corroboration of the OAuth broker working end-to-end, explicit short-lived/rotation guarantees for brokered provider tokens, and hands-on agent examples.
